title: Digitalizing carbon methodologies
challenge: Carbon methodologies live in long technical documents, which makes project design, calculation and review slow and error-prone.
did: Translate nature-based carbon methodologies into digital policies and calculation logic across Verra Project Hub and the Guardian platform (Hedera).
Lead testing and release, from requirements through QA, UAT and production.
Write API documentation and developer guides so project developers can submit data directly.
outcome: Six methodology policies taken through to release on the Guardian platform, spanning agriculture, afforestation, forest management and blue carbon.
Calculation-logic corrections that protect the accuracy of credit outcomes.

title: Connecting remote-sensing data providers to a carbon registry
challenge: Forest carbon projects increasingly rely on satellite-derived data, but that data has to flow into the registry in a consistent and auditable way.
did: Lead onboarding of remote-sensing data service providers for Verra's afforestation, reforestation and revegetation methodology (VM0047), from administrative onboarding to API integration, testing and troubleshooting.
Map provider outputs to methodology inputs and review integration results.
Wrote the product requirements for a public directory of vetted data providers.
outcome: 12+ data service providers in onboarding and integration.
Public provider directory live on Verra Project Hub; co-hosted the VM0047 onboarding webinar with Hashgraph.

title: End-to-end digital MRV for forest protection
challenge: Forest protection projects needed continuous, credible monitoring rather than infrequent field audits.
did: Designed a machine-learning and remote-sensing MRV system for near-real-time forest monitoring.
Led research on new AI and remote-sensing methodologies.
Built an API for calculating corporate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.
outcome: Contributed to Bangladesh's first carbon credit marketplace.

title: From research to product: AI yield forecasting
challenge: Forest managers needed faster, scalable yield estimates than repeated field inventories can provide.
did: Built machine-learning models that predict loblolly pine yield from UAV-LiDAR, SAR and optical satellite data.
Tested how well the models transfer across sites and over time.
Packaged the dissertation as an interactive dashboard.
outcome: Peer-reviewed results in Forest Ecology and Management, International Journal of Remote Sensing and Journal of Forestry; invited talks to industry (Weyerhaeuser) and research cooperatives.
